It unfortunately isn't easy, at least not with a game that old. A map from a recent title would be easy, as the assets are modern with really high poly counts and high texture quality, so all they'd need to do is port them into the current version of the proprietary engine (as, iirc, it changed between releases) and fix any compatibility/collision issues. With anything older than a few years ago, the assets poly count isn't high enough to even pass as current gen, so all of those assets would have to be reworked. While they do have the map designs and layouts - and old maps have undoubtedly been used as reference before - the actual meat of development is gonna come from the assets/textures, at least when it comes to specifically building out a map. And of course depending on their workflow the actual process of building an asset to shipping it in a map no doubt has some process to it that complicates things. And then of course they have to test each layout, make adjustments for balance, squash map specific bugs (as best they can) and optimize every asset they can before it can ship. With some maps where they can reuse assets from a recent release or from other parts of the game, that time is gonna shorten but it does still take a lot to make a map. And were they to, for example recreate a famous historical location from a classic title, they'd have to most likely create almost every asset from scratch, and it's very likely they wouldn't even be able to reuse that layout anyway for balance purposes.
